title: Suggamuck (Birch Creek)
summary: Suggamuck is recorded as a creek near Flanders, now called Birch Creek, one of the creeks at the west end of Peconic Bay.
history_content: The name appears in Paucamp's 1660 testimony describing bounds at the west end of Peconic Bay. It was also remembered in fishing-station work as a bass-fishing place.
translation_content:
The companion fishing-station source gives the meaning as a bass-fishing place.

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous place names are also powerful vehicles for narrating history and inscribing the landscape with meaning.”

— Christina Gray and Daniel Rück, Reclaiming Indigenous Place Names (2019), paragraph beginning ‘Just as colonial place names’
preservation_content: Suggamuck connects Birch Creek with Native fishing knowledge and the creek-by-creek geography of western Peconic Bay.
